problem.summary: 现有深度卷积神经网络（CNN）要求固定大小的输入图像（例如224×224），这一要求是人为的，可能降低对任意大小/尺度图像或子图像的识别精度。

motivation.summary: 固定输入尺寸的限制忽略了尺度变化问题，裁剪或扭曲图像会丢失信息或引入失真。CNN的卷积层本身不需要固定尺寸，但后续的全连接层需要固定长度的输入。需要一种方法来消除这一限制，同时保持或提升性能。

core_idea.summary: 在最后一个卷积层之上引入空间金字塔池化（SPP）层，对任意大小的特征图进行多尺度池化，生成固定长度的表示，从而允许网络接受任意大小的输入图像。

method.summary: 提出SPP-net网络结构，将SPP层插入卷积层和全连接层之间。SPP层使用多级金字塔（例如{6×6, 3×3, 2×2, 1×1}）对特征图进行池化，将池化后的特征拼接成固定长度的向量。训练时采用单尺寸或多尺寸训练策略。在检测任务中，对整个图像只运行一次卷积，然后对候选窗口的特征图区域进行SPP池化，提取固定长度特征用于训练检测器。

experiments.summary: 在ImageNet 2012分类、Pascal VOC 2007分类与检测、Caltech101分类以及ILSVRC 2014竞赛上进行了广泛实验。实验比较了不同CNN架构（ZF-5, Convnet*-5, Overfeat-5, Overfeat-7）有无SPP的效果，以及单尺寸训练、多尺寸训练、全图表示、多尺度检测、模型组合等策略。

claims.claim: SPP-net可以消除CNN对固定输入尺寸的要求，生成固定长度的表示。
SPP对物体形变具有鲁棒性，能提升各种CNN架构的分类精度。
在检测任务中，SPP-net只需对整个图像运行一次卷积，然后对任意窗口的特征图进行池化，比R-CNN快数十到上百倍，同时精度相当或更高。
SPP-net在ImageNet 2012、Pascal VOC 2007、Caltech101上取得了当时最优的分类结果。
在ILSVRC 2014竞赛中，基于SPP-net的方法在检测和分类任务上分别获得第2名和第3名。

limitations.limitation: 论文未详细讨论SPP层引入的额外计算开销。在检测任务中，当使用未经微调的全连接层时，性能可能下降，因为预训练是在图像区域上进行的，而检测时是在特征图区域上使用。多尺寸训练的收敛速度可能比单尺寸训练慢。

nodes.title: 输入图像
nodes.label: Input Image
nodes.summary: 任意大小和尺度的原始图像。
nodes.description: 网络接受任意尺寸的输入图像，无需裁剪或扭曲到固定大小。

nodes.title: 卷积层
nodes.label: Convolutional Layers
nodes.summary: 提取图像特征，生成特征图。卷积操作本身不依赖固定输入尺寸。
nodes.description: 由多个卷积层和池化层组成，以滑动窗口方式操作，输出特征图，其空间尺寸随输入图像大小而变化。

nodes.title: 空间金字塔池化层
nodes.label: Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP) Layer
nodes.summary: 核心创新模块。对特征图进行多尺度池化，生成固定长度的表示。
nodes.description: 位于最后一个卷积层之后。使用多级金字塔（如{6×6, 3×3, 2×2, 1×1}）对特征图进行最大池化，将各级池化结果拼接成一个固定长度的向量。这使得网络能够处理任意大小的输入。

nodes.title: 全连接层
nodes.label: Fully-Connected Layers
nodes.summary: 接收SPP层输出的固定长度特征向量，进行分类或回归。
nodes.description: SPP层输出的固定长度向量被送入全连接层，最后接softmax或其他分类器。由于输入长度固定，全连接层可以正常工作。

nodes.title: 分类输出
nodes.label: Classification Output
nodes.summary: 图像分类任务的预测结果。
nodes.description: 对于分类任务，网络输出类别概率分布。

nodes.title: 检测特征提取
nodes.label: Detection Feature Extraction
nodes.summary: 在检测任务中，对整个图像只运行一次卷积，然后对候选窗口的特征图区域进行SPP池化。
nodes.description: 对于检测任务，首先对整个图像提取卷积特征图（可能在多个尺度上）。然后，对于每个候选窗口，将其映射到特征图上对应区域，并对该区域应用SPP层，提取固定长度的特征向量用于训练检测器（如SVM）。

nodes.title: 检测输出
nodes.label: Detection Output
nodes.summary: 物体检测任务的预测边界框和类别。
nodes.description: 使用提取的特征训练二分类SVM，并可能结合边界框回归，输出检测结果。

deltas.before: 网络输入必须是固定尺寸的图像。
deltas.after: 网络可以接受任意尺寸的输入图像。
deltas.why_it_matters: 消除了人为的尺寸限制，避免了裁剪或扭曲带来的信息损失或失真，能更好地处理不同尺度和长宽比的物体。

deltas.before: 池化层（如最大池化）通常使用固定大小的窗口和步长，输出尺寸依赖于输入尺寸。
deltas.after: SPP层使用多级金字塔（如{6×6, 3×3, 2×2, 1×1}）对特征图进行池化，无论输入特征图大小如何，输出都是固定长度的向量。
deltas.why_it_matters: 实现了从任意大小特征图到固定长度表示的转换，是连接卷积层和全连接层的关键桥梁。

deltas.before: 在检测任务中，R-CNN需要对每个候选窗口（约2000个）独立运行整个CNN进行特征提取，计算非常耗时。
deltas.after: SPP-net对整个图像只运行一次卷积，然后对每个候选窗口的特征图区域进行SPP池化提取特征。
deltas.why_it_matters: 极大地提升了检测速度（论文报告比R-CNN快24-102倍），同时保持了相当的精度。

deltas.before: 训练时通常使用单一固定尺寸的图像。
deltas.after: 提出多尺寸训练策略，在训练过程中交替使用不同尺寸（如224和180）的图像，但网络参数共享。
deltas.why_it_matters: 增强了网络对尺度变化的鲁棒性，进一步提升了分类精度。

variables.name: feat
variables.description: 最后一个卷积层输出的特征图，尺寸可变。

variables.name: Pool_{level_i}
variables.description: 第i级金字塔的池化操作，通常为最大池化，窗口大小和步长根据该级网格划分确定（例如6×6, 3×3, 2×2, 1×1）。

formulas.intuition: SPP层的核心操作。它将特征图在多个空间尺度上进行池化（例如在6×6、3×3、2×2、1×1的网格上分别做最大池化），然后将所有池化结果拼接起来。这样，无论输入特征图的大小如何，输出向量的长度都是固定的（例如6*6 + 3*3 + 2*2 + 1*1 = 50个bin，乘以特征通道数）。

variables.name: x, x''
variables.description: 图像域中窗口的左/右（或上/下）边界坐标。

variables.name: x', x''
variables.description: 映射到特征图上的对应边界坐标。

variables.name: S
variables.description: 特征图相对于图像的总步长（stride）。例如，对于ZF-5在conv5上，S=16。

formulas.intuition: 在检测任务中，需要将图像域中的候选窗口映射到卷积特征图上的对应区域。这个公式描述了如何根据特征图的总步长S，将图像坐标转换为特征图坐标，并考虑了取整操作。

glossary.SPP (Spatial Pyramid Pooling): 空间金字塔池化。一种池化策略，将特征图在多个空间尺度（金字塔层级）上进行划分，并在每个划分区域内进行池化（如最大池化），最后将所有池化结果拼接起来，生成固定长度的表示。
glossary.SPP-net: 空间金字塔池化网络。本文提出的网络结构，在标准CNN的最后一个卷积层和全连接层之间插入SPP层。
glossary.Feature Map: 特征图。卷积层或池化层的输出，是一个三维张量（高度×宽度×通道数），包含了输入图像在不同空间位置的特征响应。
glossary.Fully-Connected Layer: 全连接层。神经网络中的一种层，其中每个神经元与前一层的所有神经元相连接。在CNN中，通常位于卷积层之后，用于将学习到的特征表示映射到样本标记空间。
glossary.R-CNN: Regions with CNN features。一种物体检测方法，首先生成候选区域，然后对每个区域独立运行CNN提取特征，最后用SVM分类。
glossary.Selective Search: 选择性搜索。一种图像分割和候选区域生成算法，用于物体检测中生成可能包含物体的候选窗口。
glossary.Fine-tuning: 微调。在预训练模型的基础上，使用新的数据集对网络的部分或全部参数进行进一步训练，以适应新任务。
glossary.Bounding Box Regression: 边界框回归。一种用于提高物体检测定位精度的技术，通过回归模型对候选窗口的坐标进行微调，使其更接近真实边界框。
glossary.mAP (mean Average Precision): 平均精度均值。物体检测和分类任务中常用的评估指标，计算每个类别的平均精度（AP），然后取所有类别AP的平均值。
glossary.Top-1/Top-5 Error: Top-1/Top-5错误率。图像分类任务的评估指标。Top-1错误率是指模型预测的最可能类别与真实类别不一致的比例；Top-5错误率是指真实类别不在模型预测的前5个最可能类别中的比例。
glossary.Multi-size Training: 多尺寸训练。在训练过程中，交替使用不同尺寸的输入图像（如224和180），但网络参数共享，以增强模型对尺度变化的适应性。
glossary.Single-size Training: 单尺寸训练。在训练过程中，只使用单一固定尺寸（如224×224）的输入图像。
glossary.ILSVRC: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge。一个大规模的视觉识别竞赛，包括图像分类、物体检测等任务。
glossary.Pascal VOC: Visual Object Classes Challenge。一个常用的物体检测和图像分割基准数据集和竞赛。
glossary.Caltech101: 一个包含101个物体类别的图像分类数据集。

steps.description: 1. 准备数据集：下载并预处理ImageNet 2012, Pascal VOC 2007, Caltech101等数据集。
2. 实现基础CNN架构：实现ZF-5, Convnet*-5, Overfeat-5, Overfeat-7等网络结构。
3. 实现SPP层：根据论文描述，实现多级金字塔池化（如{6×6, 3×3, 2×2, 1×1}），包括前向和反向传播。
4. 构建SPP-net：将SPP层插入到基础CNN的最后一个卷积层和全连接层之间。
5. 训练策略：实现单尺寸训练（固定224输入）和多尺寸训练（交替使用224和180输入，参数共享）。
6. 分类任务评估：在ImageNet 2012验证集上使用10-view预测评估Top-1/Top-5错误率；在Pascal VOC 2007和Caltech101上提取特征训练SVM并评估mAP/准确率。
7. 检测任务实现：实现基于SPP-net的检测流程，包括：对整个图像提取多尺度特征图；将候选窗口映射到特征图；对每个窗口的特征图区域应用SPP池化；提取特征训练二分类SVM；可选地进行边界框回归。
8. 检测任务评估：在Pascal VOC 2007测试集上评估检测mAP，并与R-CNN等方法比较速度和精度。
9. 模型组合（可选）：训练多个不同随机初始化的SPP-net模型，在检测时组合它们的预测结果。

metadata.abstract: Existing deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) require a fixed-size (e.g., 224<inline-formula><tex-math>$\times$ </tex-math><alternatives><inline-graphic xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="he-ieq1-2389824.gif"/></alternatives></inline-formula>224) input image. This requirement is “artificial” and may reduce the recognition accuracy for the images or sub-images of an arbitrary size/scale. In this work, we equip the networks with another pooling strategy, “spatial pyramid pooling”, to eliminate the above requirement. The new network structure, called SPP-net, can generate a fixed-length representation regardless of image size/scale. Pyramid pooling is also robust to object deformations. With these advantages, SPP-net should in general improve all CNN-based image classification methods. On the ImageNet 2012 dataset, we demonstrate that SPP-net boosts the accuracy of a variety of CNN architectures despite their different designs. On the Pascal VOC 2007 and Caltech101 datasets, SPP-net achieves state-of-the-art classification results using a single full-image representation and no fine-tuning. The power of SPP-net is also significant in object detection. Using SPP-net, we compute the feature maps from the entire image only once, and then pool features in arbitrary regions (sub-images) to generate fixed-length representations for training the detectors. This method avoids repeatedly computing the convolutional features. In processing test images, our method is 24-102 <inline-formula><tex-math>$\times$</tex-math><alternatives><inline-graphic xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="he-ieq2-2389824.gif"/> </alternatives></inline-formula> faster than the R-CNN method, while achieving better or comparable accuracy on Pascal VOC 2007. In ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) 2014, our methods rank #2 in object detection and #3 in image classification among all 38 teams. This manuscript also introduces the improvement made for this competition.

1 I NTRODUCTION
We are witnessing a rapid, revolutionary change in our vision community, mainly caused by deep con- volutional neural networks (CNNs) [1] and the avail-
ability of large scale training data [2]. Deep-networks-

However, there is a technical issue in the training and testing of the CNNs: the prevalent CNNs require a ﬁxed input image size ( e.g., 224×224), which limits both the aspect ratio and the scale of the input image. When applied to images of arbitrary sizes, current methods mostly ﬁt the input image to the ﬁxed size, either via cropping [3], [4] or via warping [13], [7], as shown in Figure 1 (top). But the cropped region may not contain the entire object, while the warped content may result in unwanted geometric distortion. The convo- lutional layers operate in a sliding-window manner and output feature maps which represent the spatial arrangement of the activations (Figure 2). In fact, con- volutional layers do not require a ﬁxed image size and can generate feature maps of any sizes. On the other hand, the fully-connected layers need to have ﬁxed- size/length input by their deﬁnition. Hence, the ﬁxed- size constraint comes only from the fully-connected layers, which exist at a deeper stage of the network. In this paper, we introduce a spatial pyramid pool- ing (SPP) [14], [15] layer to remove the ﬁxed-size constraint of the network. Speciﬁcally, we add an arXiv:1406.4729v4 [cs....

In other words, we perform some information “aggregation” at a deeper stage of the network hierarchy (between con- volutional layers and fully-connected layers) to avoid the need for cropping or warping at the beginning.

It partitions the image into divisions from ﬁner to coarser levels, and aggregates local features in them. SPP has long been a key component in the leading and competition-winning systems for classi- ﬁcation (e.g., [17], [18], [19]) and detection ( e.g., [20]) before the recent prevalence of CNNs. Nevertheless, SPP has not been considered in the context of CNNs. We note that SPP has several remarkable properties for deep CNNs: 1) SPP is able to generate a ﬁxed- length output regardless of the input size, while the sliding window pooling used in the previous deep networks [3] cannot; 2) SPP uses multi-level spatial bins, while the sliding window pooling uses only a single window size. 3 SPP- NET FOR IMAGE CLASSIFICATION

3.1 Experiments on ImageNet 2012 Classiﬁcation We train the networks on the 1000-category training set of ImageNet 2012. Our training algorithm follows the practices of previous work [3], [4], [36]. The im- ages are resized so that the smaller dimension is 256, and a 224×224 crop is picked from the center or the four corners from the entire image 1. The data are aug- mented by horizontal ﬂipping and color altering [3]. Dropout [3] is used on the two fully-connected layers. The learning rate starts from 0.01, and is divided by 10 (twice) when the error plateaus. Our implementation is based on the publicly available code of cuda-convnet [3] and Caffe [35]. All networks in this paper can be trained on a single GeForce GTX Titan GPU (6 GB memory) within two to four weeks.
3.1.1 Baseline Network Architectures

The advantages of SPP are independent of the con- volutional network architectures used. We investigate four different network architectures in existing pub- lications [3], [4], [5] (or their modiﬁcations), and we show SPP improves the accuracy of all these architec- tures. These baseline architectures are in Table 1 and brieﬂy introduced below: • ZF-5: this architecture is based on Zeiler and Fer- gus’s (ZF) “fast” (smaller) model [4]. The number indicates ﬁve convolutional layers. • Convnet*-5: this is a modiﬁcation on Krizhevsky et al.’s network [3]. 4 SPP- NET FOR OBJECT DETECTION

Deep networks have been used for object detection. We brieﬂy review the recent state-of-the-art R-CNN method [7]. R-CNN ﬁrst extracts about 2,000 candi- date windows from each image via selective search [20]. Then the image region in each window is warped to a ﬁxed size (227×227). A pre-trained deep network is used to extract the feature of each window. A binary SVM classiﬁer is then trained on these features for detection. R-CNN generates results of compelling quality and substantially outperforms previous meth- ods. However, because R-CNN repeatedly applies the deep convolutional network to about 2,000 windows
per image, it is time-consuming. Feature extraction is
the major timing bottleneck in testing.

Our SPP-net can also be used for object detection. We extract the feature maps from the entire image only once (possibly at multiple scales). Then we ap- ply the spatial pyramid pooling on each candidate window of the feature maps to pool a ﬁxed-length representation of this window (see Figure 5). Because
the time-consuming convolutions are only applied

once, our method can run orders of magnitude faster. Our method extracts window-wise features from regions of the feature maps, while R-CNN extracts directly from image regions. In previous works, the Deformable Part Model (DPM) [23] extracts features from windows in HOG [24] feature maps, and the Selective Search (SS) method [20] extracts from win- dows in encoded SIFT feature maps. The Overfeat detection method [5] also extracts from windows of deep convolutional feature maps, but needs to pre- deﬁne the window size. 4.1 Detection Algorithm
We use the “fast” mode of selective search [20] to generate about 2,000 candidate windows per image.
Then we resize the image such that min(w,h ) = s,

and extract the feature maps from the entire image. We use the SPP-net model of ZF-5 (single-size trained) for the time being. In each candidate window, we use a 4-level spatial pyramid (1×1, 2×2, 3×3, 6×6, totally 50 bins) to pool the features. This generates a 12,800- d (256×50) representation for each window. These representations are provided to the fully-connected layers of the network. Then we train a binary linear SVM classiﬁer for each category on these features. Our implementation of the SVM training follows [20], [7]. We use the ground-truth windows to gen- erate the positive samples. The negative samples are those overlapping a positive window by at most 30% (measured by the intersection-over-union (IoU) ratio). Any negative sample is removed if it overlaps another negative sample by more than 70%. We apply the stan-
dard hard negative mining [23] to train the SVM. This

5 C ONCLUSION

SPP is a ﬂexible solution for handling different scales, sizes, and aspect ratios. These issues are important in visual recognition, but received little consideration in the context of deep networks. We have suggested a so- lution to train a deep network with a spatial pyramid pooling layer. The resulting SPP-net shows outstand- ing accuracy in classiﬁcation/detection tasks and greatly accelerates DNN-based detection. Our studies also show that many time-proven techniques/insights in computer vision can still play important roles in deep-networks-based recognition. Mapping a Window to Feature Maps. In the detection algorithm (and multi-view testing on feature maps), a window is given in the image domain, and we use it to crop the convolutional fea- ture maps ( e.g., conv 5) which have been sub-sampled several times. So we need to align the window on the feature maps. In our implementation, we project the corner point of a window onto a pixel in the feature maps, such that this corner point in the image domain is closest to the center of the receptive ﬁeld of that feature map pixel.
